name: TROCOFAB

about:
TROCOFAB, a metal manufacturer and fabricator, was founded in 2002 by Tim Trotter in St. Louis, Missouri. Trotter, a U.S. Army veteran who previously ran a family-owned manufacturing business, began by building custom metal furniture before expanding into architectural and structural metalwork. The company’s first shop occupied 5,000 square feet downtown; it moved to a larger facility in 2007 and doubled that space in 2010, now operating from the Hill neighborhood.

The firm provides a full range of metal fabrication and manufacturing services, including water‑jet and laser cutting, MIG and TIG welding, machining, brake forming, rolling, drilling, grinding, polishing, and finishing. It also offers project management, design assistance, value engineering, 3D/2D CAD drawing, prototype building, and installation. The shop handles single‑part prototypes through multipart production runs and produces architectural features such as monumental stairs, handrail systems, canopies, awnings, and building facades.

TROCOFAB serves general contractors, subcontractors, architects, and creatives across the restaurant, hospitality, healthcare, and construction sectors. Notable projects include the Edward Jones parking garage in Maryland Heights, the Museum at the Gateway Arch in St. Louis, a coffee house in Miami Beach, and a sculpture installation at Discovery Green Park in Houston. The company is also an authorized Ultralox Interlocking® dealer.

The company emphasizes detailed planning — “detailed drawings get detailed results” — and value engineering to preserve design intent while reducing costs. Its central Midwest location enables economical shipping to major cities such as Chicago, Dallas, and Atlanta, and its full‑service subcontractor model includes on‑site installation when needed.
